title: wasteland 2: director's cut
text: WL2 has an Immersive atmosphere and quality voice acting. Weather is not dynamic nor are there day/night cycles but you will find different weather conditions in some areas. Your rangers will gain experience and levels quickly. This will make them more deadly and survivable. You will see some familiar weapons in this game. But how they are implemented is for game mechanics. While not realistic, the weapons are fun and you will want a mix of weapon types used by your team, e.g. not all using energy weapons. Energy weapons and armor... it may take some time to understand how these work. Why and when they don't work and against whom. Some question whether armor should be removed before some battles (I left mine on). While the implementation may lack refinement, it still works. Take your hits, adjust your strategy and learn to be more effective in battle. Prioritize some enemies and use you action points more effectively, e.g. move to cover and/or crouch. Friendly fire can happen so watch your line of sight. Throwing grenades to a platform above your rangers or even over a fence doesn't work. You need line of sight and to be at the same level as your enemy or above them. But grenades and rockets do go where you tell them and can be very effective. Many say there are areas that are bugged, like LA and the Bastion, maybe. You may find these comments when searching for solutions. But I question if these comments are based either upon the demo or an older revision, as they have not been updated. While there are many times you might question why you can't perform a particular action regarding a quest, they can be satisfactorily completed. There are also different methods for completing most quests. How you play and in particular who you aid in your journey has an affect not only in the end-game summary but the final battle. Do you need/want allies at the final battle or are you baddass enough to take 'em all on by yourself? Play how you like and when you have won the game, play it again!

title: weird worlds: return to infinite space
text: A couple of reviews claim that you can have experienced all the game has to offer in just a handful of playthroughs... Not true. It only takes 10-40 minutes to play through once though, so it's easy to pick up and play "just one game". But people, You can -think- you've seen it all, but there are several story branches that simply don't always unlock. There are multiple endings, and gameplay is a bit different each time around thanks to random galaxies, and 3 settings each with 3 options that decide what your starting ship is, the size of the map (and approx game length), and the density of the nebula in the universe (Which greatly dictates where you can and can't travel at the start of the game.) You can download the game's precursor, Strange Adventures in Infinite Space, from the publisher's website, if you want to get an idea of what this is all about. I'm not saying you won't tire of this game after playing it a dozen or so times, you will see repeats of items, but this is part of the charm and fun of this game--once you learn what items are out there to be found, how species will interact, you can hone a strategy that will allow you to actually 'beat' the game, by which I mean unlock and win one of the 'hidden' storylines. You can bet that most of the people giving this a thumbs-down after <10 or so hours never got this far. I have this game downloaded DRM free and on another service, so my 7 hours played here at time of writing is less than accurate, I'm probably nearer to 30 hrs. I probably have seen 95% of the game's content, still haven't beaten one specific storyline... it involves an invasion, without giving too much away. You probably won't see it on your 1st (or 2nd, or 3rd) playthrough. If you are into resource management, roguelike, trading, exploration, sci-fi, or adventure games, I say give this a shot, just maybe not at full sticker price. Whatever you do though, don't listen to the reviews bashing the game for a lack of content when they haven't given it a proper chance. I'd give it another thumb up if I could. The developer is currently working on a successfully-Kickstarted sequel called Sea of Stars, and I am one of many people who are eager to see it ship. Give these guys a shot!

text: I love so many things about this game that I don't know where to start. It has an excellent atmosphere; from the quirky bits of backstory to the memorable snippets of country music you sometimes pick up while drifting through the void, it does a great job of creating a unique 'feel'. The combat is unforgiving and forces you to truly consider the consequences of every engagement, but a bit of cleverness and careful planning can help you avoid combat entirely if you so choose (and on many runs, that's exactly what I did; combat is not by any means central to the game). I love how the various random items and their lore interconnect, and how exciting the storylines have the potential to be, in what appears on the surface to be an aimless journey. The final boss, simple as it was, is possibly the closest thing to 'epic' that I have ever seen in a game. So yes. If you like roguelikes and want to try something that is more about exploration and thinking creatively rather than just killing everything in sight, check out Weird Worlds.

title: weird worlds: return to infinite space
text: = Summary = Weird Worlds: Return to Infinite Space is a time limited rogue like space exploration game. + Keeps you interesting into discovering how to beat the game - Tutorial is unnecessarily tedious - Short game overall = Review = Your mission is to meet alien species and get items throughout space and you have a limited time to do it. Once you're happy with your exploration you may return home, retire and the game ends. When you travel to a galaxy you may either find items or aliens. Some items are useful to your exploration while others just give you points. The useful items may be weapons, shields or trusters that can be equiped. Other useful items may be used during your exploration. You may encounter friendly, neutral and hostile aliens. Friendly aliens usually just want to negotiate, neutral aliens warn you to leave and hostile aliens always engage in combat. You can engage in combat with neutral aliens, just leave them there or make peace. It is an interesting but overall short game. At first it seems like a weird game with lots of textual information but it gets very addicting once you grasp it. The tutorial is one of the worst aspects of this game. It is unnecessarily tedious and long. My advice is to ignore the tutorial altogether and just learn the game as you go. The interesting part is understanding how to explore every part of the game. For that you need to know which items are useful or not. The game is not very large however so once you beat it a few times there's not much to do besides geetting a better score. There are special events on each level so you may want to finish those as well. Anyway it is an interesting rogue like game but could have more to do.

title: wildstar
text: Time played on Steam is not accurate, I've played well over 1000 hours. It is free (and incredibly fair to free players, more so than other f2p MMOs by far.) and it's fun. Try it. What do you have to lose? Pros: - Amazing fast-paced combat, emphasising on movement and reaction time. It's hectic in a really fun way. The telegraph system makes combat very intuitive. You'll know when and why you messed up in a fight. - Double jump, dodge and sprint is part of every class and all are used in combat to really add an extra dimension. - Real physics! It's unheard of in other MMOs. You properly gain momentum when going down a slope (did I mention hoverboards?). There are areas with reduced gravity and it feels right. - Immersive lighting effects. They are not super advanced but they beat "painted directly on the texture" lighting in most MMOs. For example, there are areas where you have a helmet with a lamp on it to move around in the dark. The bundle of light points in the direction you are facing. This kind of tech does not exist in any MMO i've played and it can be really immersive. I wish they would use it more often though. - The theme breaks away from the usual medieval fantasy MMOs that we've all been playing for years. - The music is so good. - Good story. It's easy to follow if you want it to be but there's additional lore all around to learn more if that's your thing. - Free. The fairest cash shop model in any MMO I've seen and it doesn't constantly nag you to buy things. Most of the things you buy are cosmetic in nature anyway. You can earn a currency through just playing the game for free that will allow you to buy most of the items from the cash shop the same way you would with real money. - Player housing is really good. I'm not interested in it but I've played around with it and you can do a lot of creative things with it. Cons: - There are bugs. Quite a lot of the bugs are UI related. Most of the time, a quick reload of the UI can fix it and there are certain addons that fix problems in the default UI altogether. Other in game bugs exist but fixes have been improving steadily. - If you like story, it doesn't really start until lvl 30-35, but after that I really like it. - The game does not perform nearly as well as it should. Some addons have been made that improve performance. But really, get to work, Carbine. For maximum enjoyment: - Join a guild! I can't stress this enough. Just because WoW thinks making content too accessible is a good thing, doesn't mean it is. Some group content is very hard to complete with strangers, due to text chat being too slow to communicate mid-combat. If you're used to the dungeon finder in other MMOs, this is harder. Guild groups make it incredibly fun and rewarding. - Skip task quests while leveling. They're incredibly generic extra quests on top of the story/regional/world quests that usually don't give you enough of a reward. The exp is minimal and they are entirely optional. - Ignore the doomsayers. People have been saying the game is dead for 2 years now. There aren't many players but there's enough.

And DPS, well... those poor squishies better watch out for red, because there's PLENTY of red to die in. But when I was with a roleplaying guild, that was it's own very rewarding experience. text: Much like DOOM and Heretic/Hexen, Wolfenstein 3D is a classic shooter of the dos era. Everyone knows the story about how this is the grandfather of modern shooters and maybe that's why you're here, maybe you want to give this game a try. If you do you need to note this is the dos version of the game, many people hate that and for good reason too, dosbox (an emulation of dos) doesn't run well on modern machines unless you know how to alter the config files for games that run on it. Luckily, though, there are source ports for these games that allows them to run smoothly at 60fps and at higher resolutions. The source ports I use do allow you to play the games "vanilla" aside from the higher frame rate, which can be changed if you want the most vanilla experience possible while still being able to enjoy these games. I do recommend this game, but please if you get it get ecwolf.

title: wolfenstein 3d
text: One of the earliest FPS games ever made, Wolfenstein 3D has a lot of historical importance, and with a lot people playing it and having fond memories with it, its still considered a great game. Do I think its good well... Yes and no. First things first this port is crap. Its just a DOSbox shell which would be fine, but the configuration is absolute garbage. You have to do a lot of DOSBOX config changes before the game is even playable. After that you are left with a game that is fun, but only in short bursts. That isn't really a knock against the game as a whole because it was one of the earlist FPS games ever made, but rather a warning to you if you choose to buy it. Wolfenstein 3D has a lot of flaws in 2015 that weren't really apparent back in 1992. The levels are repetetive mazes that are easy to get lost in and theres no map which worsens the issue. The controls by default are clunky and hard to use (though this is fixable but not on this release alone, a source port will fix this) the game is unfairly difficult, the list goes on. But its still a really FUN game. The shooting is very fun and the 3 guns that you get in the game are all fun to use. Especially the chaingun with its loud sounds and sheer power. Killing things is really fun in this game thanks to great sound effects, good hit detection and good animation. The game is fun, but it hasn't exactly aged well, but if you can tolerate its problems Wolfenstein 3D is still a fun game. If anything you should buy for its historical importance. The visuals are basic, no surprise there, but they don't look bad. The sprites are very detailed and the textures look good. The textures do tend to repeat and the levels are complex in design but basic in look. There are no multileveled floors, the levels are flat and static, but again this game was released in 1992 so its okay. The music is really good, I love that twangy Sound Blaster\Adlib sound that many DOS games had at the time and this is no exception. The sound effects are also good. Overall I recommend this game only if you know if you are getting into. You have to know how to tweak the DOSbox config file before starting (unless you get a source port) and this game does have a lot of flaws by todays standards, but its historically important and for that reason alone you should give Wolfenstein 3D a try,

text: This isn't a native port for modern OSes, it is just an emulation using Doxbox.  This is great for pure-ists who like playing the original versions of games.  However, the controls are difficult to get used to, probably because there was no standard for FPS games at the time of this game's creation.  If you try to use a game controller, such as an Xbox 360 gamepad, then only up to four buttons will be recognized and there is no support for the sensitivity of the thumb sticks.  Everything is treated as digital input (as opposed to analog) except for the mouse.
